newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French-Belgian Dexia positive on 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: French-Belgian Dexia positive on 1997 outlook.

text.p: French-Belgian banking group Dexia said on Wednesday that it was cautiously optimistic about its 1997 earnings outlook.

"1997 so far has been a good year for Dexia. The first four months have seen a positive development in credit activities, notably in financing of local authorities on an international level and for the retail business in Belgium," said Francois Narmon, chief executive officer of the group's Belgian arm.
"We are optimistic that thanks to cost control and operational growth our earnings will develop in a favourable manner," Narmon said.
He declined to give a more precise indication of expected 1997 profit growth.
Dexia had a 1996 group net profit of 19.39 billion Belgian francs.
Narmon said however that Dexia will be able, in a few years, to boost its return on equity to 13 percent from 11.5 percent in 1996.

He said that in the first quarter of 1997, insurance products, notably life insurance, had shown strong growth, as well as the fund management and private banking activities of Dexia unit Banque Internationale a Luxembourg (BIL).
He also said the favourable earnings outlook for 1997 was partly based on the first tangible effects of the synergies between the French and Belgian operations of the group.
